summary: AC14 grep gate is GREEN (zero matches across all three files). Task 11's Virtual Threads section is untouched. Per-bullet rewrites mostly land cleanly against the post-flip source files (SecurityConfig, RememberMeCookieSerializer, AuthService, EmailService, ProjectService, TelegramApiClient, BotService, GlobalErrorHandler, ConcurrencyTestUtils all match). Two real findings remain: (1) one source-mirage in patterns.md — the Project Workspace block still says `pathMatchers("/api/**")` where the post-flip SecurityConfig uses `requestMatchers(...)` (this is a reactive WebFlux API name and contradicts the Spring Security MVC heading the same task added 30 lines above); (2) deployment.md Local Development still says `Netty :8080` in the gradle-run hint where post-flip Tomcat is the embedded server. Neither is in the AC14 grep gate but both contradict the post-flip stack the task is meant to align the docs with.

findings.issue: The bullet still cites `SecurityConfig pathMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()` — `pathMatchers(...)` is the reactive `ServerHttpSecurity` API and does not exist in the post-flip `SecurityConfig.java`. The post-flip source (lines 91-98) uses `requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()`. This is the Servlet-stack name the same task established 30+ lines above in the Spring Security MVC rewrite (`pathMatchers(...)` → `requestMatchers(...)` swap is explicit in task instructions for line ~40-46). The token does not match the AC14 grep alternation (which catches `WebFlux`, not the matcher API name), so it slipped through, but it is a clear mirage: a future onboarding agent reading this bullet would call a method that does not exist on `HttpSecurity`.
findings.fix: Replace `pathMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()` with `requestMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()` on patterns.md line 154. Same Servlet-stack name swap already applied in the rewritten Spring Security MVC heading above.

findings.issue: Local Development gradle-run hint reads `cd backend && ./gradlew bootRun  # Netty :8080 (Spring DevTools hot-reload)`. Netty is the WebFlux reactive server; the post-flip stack uses embedded Tomcat (driven by `spring-boot-starter-web`, confirmed in architecture.md line 27). The comment misleads anyone reading deployment.md about the runtime model the same Wave-3 task is meant to align docs around. Not an AC14 grep token but a clear post-flip stale reference flagged by the task's `sweep for any stray reactive token` directive (deployment.md section 5).
findings.fix: Change the inline comment to `# Tomcat :8080 (Spring DevTools hot-reload)` (the embedded servlet container on the MVC + virtual-threads stack).
